vulnerability_analysis: The PlentyCoin contract has three owner-only functions (setTaxFeePercent, setLiquidityFeePercent, setMaxTxPercent) that modify critical tokenomics parameters (_taxFee, _liquidityFee, _maxTxAmount) without emitting any events. This allows a malicious owner to silently change fees or transaction limits without users or monitoring systems being able to detect these changes on-chain. The oracle checks if _taxFee was modified without a corresponding event.
attack_strategy: 1. Impersonate the contract owner using vm.startPrank(). 2. Record the initial _taxFee value. 3. Call setTaxFeePercent() to modify the tax fee. 4. Verify the state changed but no TaxFeeUpdated event was emitted. This demonstrates the missing event log vulnerability.
step_by_step_plan: 1. Create interface for the Plenty contract with the vulnerable functions. 2. In setUp(), initialize the contract instance and label addresses. 3. In testExploit(), get the owner address, record initial _taxFee, impersonate owner, call setTaxFeePercent() with a new value, verify the state changed. 4. Use assertGt to confirm the tax fee was modified (oracle check).
